# Decision history — save-your-skin

Every revision of every decision, plus the terminal revisions of other normative records. Includes archived records: this is the project's memory of what it used to think.

## lege.decision.renderer-boundary

### Revision 2 — The viewer consumes a frame snapshot

`active` · `@lege.decision.renderer-boundary/2` · scope `path "lege/**"` · topic `renderer-boundary`

The viewer reads an immutable frame snapshot produced by the simulator at each
tick boundary. It does not call into the simulator, and no engine type appears
in a viewer signature.

**Context.** Revision 1 put engine types in viewer signatures and made the viewer untestable in isolation. The text-layout question turned on the same boundary, so both were settled together.

**Consequences.** One extra allocation and copy per frame, measured at 0.4 ms against the 16 ms budget. Accepted. The snapshot type is now a third thing to keep in step when simulator state changes, which the tandem-work policy already covers.

**Retired claims** — `#direct-calls`, dropped at this revision.

**supersedes** `@lege.decision.renderer-boundary/1`

### Revision 1 — The viewer calls the simulator directly

`superseded` · `@lege.decision.renderer-boundary/1` · scope `path "lege/**"` · topic `renderer-boundary`

The viewer calls simulator entry points directly at each tick boundary and
reads state through them.

**Context.** Chosen for the walking skeleton, when there was no frame snapshot to read and no second consumer of simulator state.

**superseded by** `@lege.decision.renderer-boundary/2`

## sim.decision.timestep-4ms

### Revision 1 — Fix the simulator timestep at 4 ms

`proposed` · `@sim.decision.timestep-4ms/1` · scope `path "sim/src/step.rs"` · topic `timestep-length`

The simulator steps at 4 ms, giving four steps per rendered frame at 60 Hz.

**Context.** The current 8 ms step is visible as input latency in the day loop. 4 ms halves it and doubles the per-frame simulation cost.

**Consequences.** Four steps per frame instead of two. Whether that fits the frame budget is exactly what is unresolved, which is why this is still a proposal.

## sys.decision.view-generation

### Revision 1 — Views are generated and committed

`active` · `@sys.decision.view-generation/1` · scope `path "docs/generated/**"` · topic `view-generation`

`akr build` writes the six generated views into docs/generated, and those files
are committed. CI runs `akr check --views-current` and fails on any difference.

**Context.** The alternative was generating views on demand and gitignoring them, which would leave anyone reading the repository on the web with nothing.

**Consequences.** Regenerated views conflict on merge. The conflict is always resolved by rebuilding, never by hand-merging, and that procedure belongs in AGENTS.md.
